answer: Before bidding, each agent must lock a deposit in a public contract. A pulse of signed bids lets auditors prove when an agent has submitted conflicting bids for the same task, triggering a slash of that agent’s deposit. A cipher protects the bid contents, while signatures establish accountability; even a sonnet-writing bot must escrow funds. An attacker creating many identities must lock capital for each one, and proven equivocation destroys part of it.
